boundaries: This notice is communication evidence only. It neither selects an option nor grants approval, execution authority, lifecycle effect, promotion, or publication authority.

FSP-01 proves only current theorem-in-model witnesses under exact source, model, assumptions, targets, toolchain, dependency resolution, and observed axioms; it does not prove runtime agreement, security, general conformance, or that an agent satisfies a specification.
Keep DomainSpec semantics, CAV2 authority semantics, and Lean model/proof ownership distinct. A Lean repair cannot invent or silently merge owner-local meaning.
Exclude approved-source adapters and translation from FSP-02; those are FSP-03 concerns.
Exclude binding to the real CAV2 graph from FSP-02; that is an FSP-04 concern after adapters exist.

Exclude Cedar, Datalog, runtime evaluator execution, DecisionMatchesSpec implementation, live enforcement, deployment, and release from FSP-02; bounded Cedar or Datalog evaluation belongs no earlier than FSP-05.
Do not reuse the FSP-01 explicit-zero route or receipts for an FSP-02 no-repair decision. A fresh owner decision and, if needed, a separately governed FSP-02 route are required.
The underlying FSP-01 run evidence is currently a local candidate reference; sharing this notice does not promote that evidence or make its source artifacts remotely available.
key_points: Observed result: all six selected declarations built in fresh isolated copies; there were no failures, skips, blocked rows, sorry/admit matches, or source changes. The result is theorem-in-model evidence only.

Decision principle: FSP-02 is described by the planning evidence as a Lean repair stage. A nonzero scope should therefore be justified by one named theorem proposition, assumption, target, or model-shape blocker, not merely by the bounded claim ceilings of correct existing theorems.

Option A — no Lean repair, evidence-favored default: Victor records that no identified Lean defect blocks the next separately gated phase. Preserve all six current propositions and ceilings. This is a fresh owner decision; the FSP-01 explicit-zero mechanism cannot be reused because no FSP-02 zero route currently exists.

Option B — DomainSpec-v2 permission-kernel repair: narrowly strengthen or expose assumptions around AgentPermissionKernel.decidePolicy_sound, deny_precedence, or layered_not_flattenable. Example candidate: make matcher adequacy an explicit hypothesis for a bounded typed policy fragment. This remains theorem-in-model and cannot claim runtime enforcement, security, matcher implementation correctness, or DomainSpec-v2 conformance.

Option C — synthetic CAV2 graph-theorem repair: narrowly strengthen the model-local acyclicity surface beyond the current fixed three-node witness. Example candidate: an owner-selected finite-graph proposition about cycle detection or the insufficiency of node-local predicates. It must remain synthetic and must not bind the real CAV2 graph, which belongs no earlier than FSP-04.

Option D — functorial-residue repair: narrowly strengthen FunctorialResidue.DiamondNonVacuity.lanPackaging_obligation_landed into an exact parameterized lemma under named categorical assumptions. Select this only if Victor identifies a concrete downstream blocker; it must not be reported as general residue or live-system conformance.

Current DomainSpec-v2 evidence supports only allow-implies-Satisfies in the local LayeredPolicy model, deny precedence in the local list model, and one concrete non-flattenability counterexample. It does not prove live authorization enforcement or the correctness of caller-supplied matcher semantics.

Current CAV2 evidence supports only a fixed three-node witness where local lints pass while the relation cycles, plus a finite-model impossibility for a node-data-only unary predicate. It is not bound to the real CAV2 graph and is not a general graph-language expressiveness result.

Recommended disposition: choose Option A unless Victor can identify one exact blocker. If a blocker exists, select exactly one of B, C, or D and bind its proposition, source ownership, target, assumptions, validation, and theorem-in-model claim ceiling before any work pack is authored.

Later-stage separation: FSP-03 owns approved-source adapters, FSP-04 owns real-graph binding, and FSP-05 may evaluate Cedar or Datalog only after FSP-03 and FSP-04. None of those effects belongs in FSP-02.
